newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Dollar vols subdued as spot rates steady.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Dollar vols subdued as spot rates steady.

text.p: Dollar options implied volatilities eased in morning Europe with spot holding overnight ranges around 1.73 marks and 114 yen.
The firmer dollar/yen spot has pushed one-month vols down to 12.0/12.5 percent from 12.3/12.6 percent late Thursday in Europe and well below this week's highs over 15 percent.

"The lower vols and the ranging spot brought out some dollar put buyers overnight," said a UK bank dealer. "Things are the calmest they've been this week, but we've still got the EU summit and the G7 coming up so these vol levels can be seen as a good time to get protection."
The European Union summit in Amsterdam starts on Monday and the G7 meeting in Denver kicks off next Friday.
Dollar/yen risk reversals have eased from this week's extreme bias for yen calls but the one-month 25 delta reversal is still seen as fairly high at 1.6/2.0 percent.
Dealers said this highlighted market caution over downside risk despite spot's recovery above the 114 yen level.

Dollar/mark implied volatilities were also softer as spot kept to ranges around 1.73 marks. One-month vol stood at 9.0/9.3 percent from 9.3/9.5 percent Thursday. The risk reversal, the difference in implied volatility between calls relative to puts, continued to trade around par.

Nerves were calmer over Europe's monetary union timetable but caution remained. Dealers said the ongoing buying of longer-dated, out-of-the-money mark calls versus the EMS bloc, especially within the interbank market, continued.
"These options, especially mark/lira, are very cheap and offer the best risk-reward for any upset to EMU," said a U.S. bank dealer. "It's a good, cheap punt."

Mark cross vols were steady in morning trade with one-month mark/French franc at 2.0/2.3 percent and mark/lira at 4.8/5.1. Although EMU timetable concerns have calmed, the risk reversals remain heavily weighted to mark calls.
